subtitulo: Phrasal verbs whose meaning has drifted
descripcion: At C2 you handle three-part phrasal verbs and the ones with a figurative meaning that has drifted far from their literal parts: come up against, get away with, look down on. Their idiomatic sense must be learned as a fixed unit; the literal words no longer help.

ejemplos.texto: The proposal came up against fierce resistance from the board.
He somehow got away with it, against all odds.
She never looked down on anyone, regardless of their background.

notas: The three parts of these verbs never separate, unlike the two-part verbs common at lower levels.
The figurative meaning is now fully detached from the literal words — look down on has nothing to do with physical height.
These verbs are frequent in speech and informal writing but sound wrong translated literally into a formal register.

es.en: Spanish has no equivalent class of verb and often needs a whole phrase for the same nuance («salirse con la suya» – get away with it). Spanish speakers at C2 understand these verbs when reading but rarely produce them without targeted practice.
es.es: El español no tiene una clase equivalente de verbos y a menudo necesita una expresión completa para el mismo matiz («salirse con la suya» – «get away with it»). Los hispanohablantes de C2 entienden estos verbos al leer, pero rara vez los producen sin práctica específica.

de.en: German separable verbs are structurally similar, so phrasal verbs feel natural to German speakers («davonkommen» – get away). The trap is particles that look alike but mean something else («auskommen» means get by, not come out).
de.de: Deutsche trennbare Verben sind strukturell ähnlich, daher fühlen sich «phrasal verbs» für Deutschsprachige natürlich an («davonkommen» – «get away»). Die Falle sind Partikeln, die ähnlich aussehen, aber etwas anderes bedeuten («auskommen» heißt «get by», nicht «come out»).

it.en: Italian has its own «verbi sintagmatici» («andare avanti» – go on, «tirare fuori» – bring out, «mettere giù» – put down), so the idea of verb + particle is familiar. Italian speakers can build on these to produce English phrasal verbs more actively.
it.it: L'italiano ha i propri verbi sintagmatici («andare avanti» – «go on», «tirare fuori» – «bring out», «mettere giù» – «put down»), quindi l'idea verbo + particella è familiare. Si può sfruttarla per produrre più attivamente i «phrasal verbs» inglesi.

fr.en: French has no particle verbs and relies on Latinate verbs that are transparent in English («tolérer» – tolerate rather than put up with). French speakers therefore understand phrasal verbs but tend to avoid them in production.
fr.fr: Le français n'a pas de verbes à particule et s'appuie sur des verbes latins transparents en anglais («tolérer» – «tolerate» plutôt que «put up with»). Les francophones comprennent donc les «phrasal verbs» mais ont tendance à les éviter en production.

pt.en: Portuguese has no particle verbs, but many verb + preposition idioms («dar com» – come across, «dar-se com» – get on with). These are a useful model for learning English phrasal verbs as fixed units.
pt.pt: O português não tem «particle verbs», mas possui muitas expressões verbo + preposição («dar com» – «come across», «dar-se com» – «get on with»). Elas são um bom modelo para aprender «phrasal verbs» ingleses como unidades fixas.

errores: Trying to split a three-part phrasal verb, which never happens.
Interpreting the verb literally instead of by its drifted figurative sense.
Using a three-part phrasal verb in a register too formal for it.

es: «*soportar*» rendered as *support* instead of *put up with*.
de: «*nicht ausstehen können*» rendered as *can't stand out* instead of *can't stand* or *can't put up with*.
it: «*sopportare*» rendered as *support* instead of *put up with*.
fr: «*supporter*» rendered as *support* instead of *put up with*.
pt: «*suportar*» rendered as *support* instead of *put up with*.

to delay acting on something deliberately

redemittel.expresion: The phrasal is the natural choice here.
redemittel.funcion: defends the informal option on register grounds

mision.consigna: Write about a company that got away with greenwashing for years.
requisitos: five figurative phrasal verbs, two with three parts
no Latinate substitute where the phrasal is the natural choice
use *greenwashing*, *carbon offsetting* and *to pay lip service to*

microtareas.texto: Ten three-part phrasal verbs: write the literal parts and the actual meaning.
Three sentences about companies that *look down on* critics.
Record 2 minutes on *carbon offsetting*: who *gets away with* what?

autochequeo: Have I kept every three-part verb unsplit?
Does the meaning match the figurative sense, not the literal words?
Does the register fit an informal or neutral context, not a very formal one?
Have I used at least four different three-part verbs?
Would a native speaker recognise this as natural, idiomatic English?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on advanced three-part phrasal verbs. Check that they remain unsplit and that the figurative meaning is used correctly. Do not rewrite the text.
